record.title: Niger COVID land-passenger restriction, March 2020 to June 2021 permission
record.scope: National land-border passenger restriction with goods exemption
record.crossings: All land posts in the order; later transport reporting specifically discusses the Mali route
record.direction: National land-border restriction; detailed direction and practice at every post not established.
record.movement: Ordinary passenger journeys and international road passenger transport.
record.exceptions: Transport of goods explicitly exempt; additional individual permissions not exhaustively reconstructed.
record.enforcement: Later operator and passenger interviews describe curtailed formal transport and clandestine alternatives.
record.consequences: Disrupted international bus services; travellers described longer and more costly informal journeys.
record.relationship: Distinct from Niger coup/ECOWAS regimes W-014 through W-017 and the February 2021 electoral overlay R2-AF-005. Overlaps neighbouring health policies, whose shared-frontier days must not be added together.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.context: The 17 March Council decision specified a later effective date. June 2021 permission was followed by uneven international service resumption depending on neighbouring policies.
record.uncertainty: Start preserves the stated 19 March midnight date without resolving its clock-boundary convention. ANP’s later 17 March retrospective is the decision date. June 17 is legal permission, not universal bilateral traffic restoration.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. Order-to-permission chronology only; neither continuous universal passenger enforcement nor simultaneous bilateral reopening is established.
